findings.claim: The analysis contradicts Goal 4 by allowing `cross_model_check: unverified-producer-unknown` instead of enforcing `KBD_PRODUCER_MODEL` so it can never occur.
findings.evidence: Phase goal: "Enforce KBD_PRODUCER_MODEL at both creator entry points so cross_model_check can never record unverified-producer-unknown". Analysis says: "No default. An unknown producer must stay unknown and be RECORDED as unknown" and acceptance includes: "When it does not → `cross_model_check: unverified-producer-unknown`, not a synthesized pass."
findings.suggested_fix: Either make creator entry points fail before dispatch when `KBD_PRODUCER_MODEL` is absent, or revise the phase goal explicitly; do not leave the plan to implement behavior opposite to the stated goal.

findings.claim: The sycophancy-gate placement remains internally contradictory, leaving the plan unable to know whether enforcement belongs in `validate-skill.sh` or in the creator.
findings.evidence: Section 6a says: "`validate-skill.sh` invokes the existing `check-findings-sycophancy.sh` as an 8th check group." Section 7 later says: "sycophancy gate placement | Creator calls the existing `check-findings-sycophancy.sh`... Do not duplicate the logic inside `validate-skill.sh`." The phase goal specifically requires: "Promote the sycophancy pass ... to an enforced gate in validate-skill.sh."
findings.suggested_fix: Make the recommendation single-source: `validate-skill.sh` is the enforced gate and shells out to `check-findings-sycophancy.sh`; creators should invoke `validate-skill.sh`, not call the sycophancy helper independently.

findings.claim: The review-loop blocking semantics are inconsistent with both the required 2-rejection cap and the claim that only one judge call is needed.
findings.evidence: Phase goal: "Make the review gate blocking on CRITICAL findings, with the existing 2-rejection cap so it cannot loop forever." Analysis says for Goal 1: "A CRITICAL finding routes to `loop_execute`" but also says "Only the final artifact of the loop is reviewed ... so a 3-iteration creation costs one judge call, not three." If a CRITICAL routes back to Execute, the artifact must be reviewed again to verify "no CRITICAL remains"; if it is not reviewed again, the gate is not blocking.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the adversarial-review retry loop explicitly: review, fix on CRITICAL, re-review, stop after the 2-rejection cap with documented behavior. Update the cost model accordingly.
